title: Creative Agencies That Also Run Your Meta Ads (2026 Guide)
summary: Compare creative agencies that also run Meta campaigns, with Knowlify first and each provider's published scope and prices. Facts checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
## Which agencies combine creative and campaigns?


The providers below publish pages that describe both halves of the job, though each packages them differently. Our[Meta ads agency comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-meta-ads-agencies-2026) covers agencies whose main job is campaign management.


### Brighter Click: real creators plus a Facebook ads service


Brighter Click sells fixed batches of creator UGC: $4,500 for 12 edited videos from 4 creators. The 12-video package takes 10 to 14 business days, and it lists full usage rights in perpetuity. On its[Facebook ads agency page](https://www.brighterclick.com/facebook-ads-agency) it also sells Facebook and Instagram campaign management, so creative and media can sit with one team. By our own arithmetic, the batch works out to about $375 per edited video.


**Consider it when** you need real creators on camera and a known price for a known number of edited videos.


### inBeat: creators and Meta management from one team


inBeat's[UGC agency page](https://inbeat.agency/ugc-agency) describes sourcing creators for fit, writing hooks and scripts, and running whitelisted ads through creator handles, with usage rights defined before production begins. Its[paid social page](https://inbeat.agency/paid-social-agency) describes weekly creative testing cycles and says it typically plans 8 to 15 new concepts a month, with 2 to 4 variations of each. Pricing is not published, and a free audit is offered.


**Consider it when** you want creator-led ads and campaign management in one team, and the creators matter more than AI formats.


### MetaAdsAgency: a flat fee for a fixed creative count


MetaAdsAgency charges a flat monthly fee for creative, testing and media buying, with 12, 30 or 60 new creatives a month by plan, starting at $2,400 a month billed yearly. It runs the ads in your own ad account and says it is independent of Meta.


**Consider it when** you want a fixed monthly creative count with management. Ask whether the creatives are new concepts or variants of one idea.


### Chamber Media: creative, strategy and management with a stated floor


Chamber Media's performance creative page lists short-form video under 60 seconds for Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, plus UGC and static ads, and its Facebook marketing page describes ad buyers and production teams working together. Its homepage FAQ says to expect around $5K to $10K a month at minimum for creative, strategy and management. It says growth is difficult on less than $5K a month in media for local brands, or $15K for national brands.


**Consider it when** your media budget clears that floor and you want to own your ad accounts.


### Voy Media: full-service Facebook and Instagram ads


Voy Media describes full-service Facebook and Instagram ads with a dedicated account manager and lead strategist, plus retargeting, custom audiences and dynamic product ads. Its[Creative Studio page](https://voymedia.com/services/creative-studio/) lists native UGC, at-home creators and full studio production. The pricing page publishes no figures and says packages depend on total ad spend, optimizations and growth.


**Consider it when** you sell in ecommerce or lead generation and want one account team across media and creative. Ask for the package scope in writing before you compare.


### Darkroom: a growth team for larger consumer brands


Darkroom's performance creative service delivers static, motion, UGC and AI formats every two weeks, with 250 to 600 production-ready assets per cycle. Its homepage says the best fit is mid-market and enterprise consumer brands, typically $10M to $500M in revenue, and that the fit is poor for single-channel brands and companies under roughly $5M. Paid media is a standard retainer plus a percentage of media, starting at $1,500 a month depending on channels.


**Consider it when** you sell through several channels and your revenue sits in that range.


## When creative only is the better choice


Some agencies make the ads and leave the media to you.[The UGC Agency](https://theugc.agency/) says it makes the ads and your team or agency runs them, although it sets up creator-handle ads. If your media buyer already runs the account, a creative-only provider can be the cleaner choice. For the trade-offs between the two models, read our[creative service versus full-service Meta agency comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/creative-service-vs-full-service-meta-agency) .


Performance-fee deals need the same care.[TubeScience](https://tubescience.com/) describes a pay-for-performance model and also advertises media buying, but its FAQ says teams not prepared to scale spend to seven figures monthly may be a weaker fit, with exceptions. A performance-linked fee is not automatically a low-commitment pilot, so ask about eligibility and payment triggers first.


## What to check before you sign with a combined agency


- **Concepts, not files.** Ask how many distinct concepts an agency delivers each month, separate from cut-downs and hook swaps. Meta expects the creative count in its systems to keep growing, so a file count tells you little.
- **Account ownership.** Chamber Media says clients own their ad accounts, and MetaAdsAgency says it runs ads in your own ad account. Ask any combined agency to name who holds the account and who has admin access.
- **Delivery format.** Meta's[Reels guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) recommends 9:16 video with audio and key messages kept inside the safe zone, clear of the Reels interface, and says Reels play with sound on unless the viewer turns it off. Add captions anyway.
- **AI labels.**[Meta's transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI features. It also says it will detect ads edited with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label, though the post does not say that detection is live yet. Plan for the label if an agency uses AI video.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for one team that makes finished AI video ads and can run the Meta campaigns, or deliver creative only.
- Combined agencies sell very different scopes, from real creators to managed AI video with a separate media service.
- Compare concept counts, account ownership, 9:16 captioned delivery and AI labeling before you compare prices.
- Price only comparable scope: a $4,500 creator batch and a $1,500 retainer plus a media share buy different work.


## FAQ


### Who is the best creative agency that also runs Meta ads?


Knowlify is our top pick for teams that want finished AI video ads and, if they choose, Meta campaign management. Brighter Click and inBeat fit better when real creators must appear on camera. Compare the concept count, the account owner and the delivery format in writing before you choose.


### Do I need one agency for creative and campaigns?


No. Creative only works well when your own media buyer already runs the account and needs a steady supply of finished ads. One agency for both can simplify testing, but confirm who decides which concepts go next.


### Who should own the ad account when one agency does both?


You should, and you should ask for that in writing. Chamber Media says clients own their ad accounts, and MetaAdsAgency says it runs ads in your own ad account, which are fair baselines to request from any agency. Also name the admins and the person who sets the test budget.


### What does an agency that does both cost?


Published figures vary widely. Brighter Click lists $4,500 for 12 edited creator videos, MetaAdsAgency starts at $2,400 a month billed yearly, Chamber Media says to expect about $5K to $10K a month at minimum, and Darkroom starts at $1,500 a month plus a percentage of media. Knowlify quotes on request, so compare the scope each price buys.


### Is a performance-fee deal a safe pilot?


Not automatically. TubeScience describes pay-for-performance production and says teams not ready to scale spend to seven figures monthly may be a weaker fit. Ask about eligibility, payment triggers and testing obligations before you sign.
